subject: How to simulate item responses from multidimensional partial credit model?

messages.author: d441408e1bd05e38
messages.subject: How to simulate item responses from multidimensional partial credit model?
parts:
using some of code you posted to this group,

library(mvtnorm)
library(mirt)

abilities <- rmvnorm(500, sigma = matrix(c(1, .4, .4, 1), 2))  
a<- matrix(c(rep(1, 10), rep(0,20), rep(1,10)), 20)
diffs <- t(apply(matrix(runif(20*4, .3, 1), 20), 1, cumsum)); 
diffs <- -(diffs - rowMeans(diffs)); 
d <- diffs + rnorm(20)
d <- t(apply(d,1,sort, decreasing=TRUE))
polytomous <- simdata(a, d, 500, Theta=abilities, itemtype = 'gpcm')  

since PCM model is a special case of GPCM models, I think I need to fix some of parameters using some options like gpcm_mats. What part should I change?

Thank you,

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: How to simulate item responses from multidimensional partial credit model?
parts:
This is the format for a graded response model, not a gpcm. The slopes are correct though in that they must be 1's. You need only create a matrix of intercepts (where the intercepts don't need to be ordered) in order to simulate these data. See the itemtype(shiny=TRUE) GUI for understanding how the intercept values work in the gpcm. 

Phil

messages.subject: Re: How to simulate item responses from multidimensional partial credit model?
parts:
Hi Phil, 
I experimented with itemplot(shiny=TRUE) to see how intercepts work for gpcm model.
I generated responses from multidimensional partial credit model. Generating item response part seemed went well using 'simdata' function. 

I tried to manipulate intercept values to have all traditional IRT parameters (b values) ordered so all scores category values can be observed. 
When I estimated item parameters using 'mirt' function, I got an error message. could you help me figure out what went wrong? 
If I removed 'start' and 'fixed' parts then no error message. 

library(mirt)
library(mvtnorm)

#itemplot(shiny=TRUE)

nitem <- 20
nperson <- 500
cor.value <- .5

s1 <-runif(nitem,-2,-1)
s2 <-runif(nitem,-.5,.5)
s3 <-runif(nitem,1,2)

d0 <- rep(0,nitem)
d1 <- d0-s1
d2 <- d1-s2
d3 <- d2-s3

d.matrix <- cbind(d0,d1,d2,d3)


abilities <- rmvnorm(nperson, sigma = matrix(c(1, cor.value, cor.value, 1), 2))  
a<- matrix(c(rep(1, nitem/2), rep(NA,nitem), rep(1,nitem/2)),nitem)

mpcm <- simdata(a,d.matrix,nperson, itemtype='gpcm',Theta=abilities)


s.input <- '
    F1 = 1-10
    F2 = 11-20
    COV = F1*F2
    start=(1-10,a1,1.0),(11-20,a2,1.0)
    fixed=(1-10,a1),(11-20,a2)'

model<- mirt.model(s.input)
model.output <-mirt(mpcm,model,itemtype="gpcm")

Error in tmp2[1L]:tmp2[2L] : NA/NaN argument
In addition: Warning message:
In model.elements(model = model, itemtype = itemtype, factorNames = factorNames,  :
  NAs introduced by coercion

You need only create a matrix of intercepts (where the intercepts don't need to be ordered) in order to simulate these data. See the itemtype(shiny=TRUE) GUI for understanding how the intercept values work in the gpcm. 

Phil
